The two bugs are confirmed by reading `stats/stats.go` against `stats/stats_test.go`:
1. **`Mean`** loops from `i := 1`, skipping `values[0]`. This makes `TestMean/single` (`{7}` → wants `7`, gets `0`) and `TestMean/several` (`{2,4,6}` → wants `4`, gets `3.33`) fail.
2. **`Max`** initializes `largest` to the zero value `0` instead of `values[0]`. This makes `TestMax/all_negative` (`{-3,-1,-7}` → wants `-1`, gets `0`) fail.

Both bugs are independent, in different functions, with no shared code path — they can be fixed in parallel by two engineers, or trivially by one. I'm splitting them into two small independent beads since that's the natural unit of "one bug, one fix, one test to satisfy," and it lets the two fixes be reviewed/landed independently.

This makes TestMean/single fail (Mean([]float64{7}) returns 0 instead of 7) and TestMean/several fail (Mean([]float64{2,4,6}) returns 3.33 instead of 4). Change the loop to start at index 0 (or otherwise include the first element) so the mean is computed over all values. Do not change Mean's signature, the empty-input handling, or any other function.
beads.acceptance: go test ./... passes for TestMean (all subtests: empty, single, several) with no other test regressions; stats.Mean sums every element of its input including index 0; no other files or functions are modified.

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 for all-negative inputs
beads.description: In stats/stats.go, Max initializes `largest` to the zero value (`var largest float64`) before scanning, so when every input value is negative, largest never gets updated and Max incorrectly returns 0 instead of the true (least negative) maximum. This makes TestMax/all_negative fail (Max([]float64{-3,-1,-7}) returns 0 instead of -1). Fix by seeding largest from the first element of values (the empty-slice case is already handled earlier by the ErrEmpty check) before the scan loop. Do not change Max's signature, its error handling, or any other function.
beads.acceptance: go test ./... passes for TestMax (all subtests: single, positive, all negative) and TestMaxEmpty with no other test regressions; stats.Max returns the correct maximum for slices containing only negative numbers; no other files or functions are modified.
